PERMANENT_REPORTING_RULE.form: CES_end_to_end = P(required evidence survives the compressor) x P(S2 succeeds | it survived)
PERMANENT_REPORTING_RULE.rule: For ANY compression mechanism, never report conditional selector performance alone. Always pair coverage after compression with conditional performance, and report the end-to-end composition.
PERMANENT_REPORTING_RULE.scope: applies to G1_TYPED_PATH, G2, and every future compression or traversal mechanism
PERMANENT_REPORTING_RULE.why: B4 proved conditional metrics can lie. P2 at M=25 posted 0.785 selected-CES-given-working at cal_3000 -- the best single number in the table -- while having discarded half the required evidence before S2 ever saw it. End-to-end it merely matched plain k=50. The conditional metric RISES as a compressor throws evidence away, so reporting it alone rewards exactly the failure it should expose.

DESIGN_FLAW_IDENTIFIED_IN_THE_FROZEN_UTI.derivable_a_priori: This is a mathematical property of the lexicographic choice, computable from the frozen definition and the observed token ranges WITHOUT reference to any policy result. It should have been derived when PHASE_0 was written and was not. Recorded as an error in protocol design, not as a data-dependent discovery.
DESIGN_FLAW_IDENTIFIED_IN_THE_FROZEN_UTI.flaw: The strictly-lexicographic realization U = Q - EPSILON*C/C_REF bounds the maximum attainable Delta_U_gate at EPSILON * (max achievable token saving) / C_REF ~= 0.01 * 62 / 1000 ~= 0.0006. Even a PERFECT oracle beats the best fixed policy by only +0.0007 under this utility. That is far below what a grouped bootstrap over 11 families can resolve, so the promotion criterion is very nearly unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION.
DESIGN_FLAW_IDENTIFIED_IN_THE_FROZEN_UTI.second_and_deeper_consequence: The same compression makes accepting almost never rational for a fitted classifier: a false ACCEPT forfeits a full quality point (1.0) while a correct ACCEPT saves ~0.0006 utility, so expected-value reasoning drives the model to escalate unless it is ~99.9% certain memory cannot help. P3 converging to always-escalate is therefore the CORRECT response to the objective as frozen -- the controller is not at fault, the objective is.
DESIGN_FLAW_IDENTIFIED_IN_THE_FROZEN_UTI.what_is_NOT_being_done: EPSILON is NOT being retuned, and the lambda_T grid is NOT being promoted to a criterion. Either move would be exactly the post-hoc tuning this project's discipline forbids. No promotion claim is made from any of this, and no GPU has been spent on PHASE_4/5.

FROZEN_CONCLUSION.statement: Direct-generation confidence carries measurable information about the value of external-memory escalation, but under the frozen quality-preservation objective it captures only a small fraction of the available cost-saving opportunity. At zero observed quality loss, the confidence-only gate reduces token cost by approximately 1.4%, compared with approximately 40% for the oracle policy. The confidence-only branch was therefore not advanced to confirmation.

the_result_that_was_banked_instead.why_this_is_the_stronger_result: It is a property of the information available to the controller, not of one run's luck landing at 1.97% versus 2.03% quality loss. It is stable, mechanistic, and it names what is missing.

FROZEN_CONCLUSION.why_NOT_FAILED: No prospective confirmation test was ever run, so no prospective test was failed. The branch is closed on a measured frontier, not on a rejected hypothesis. Calling it FAILED would misrepresent what happened and would also understate the positive content: the probe demonstrably carries signal (4/5 features clear the frozen separation threshold, |Cohen's d| up to 0.56).
FROZEN_CONCLUSION.why_not_advanced: The best available operating point consumed 98.5% of the permitted quality-loss budget (0.0197 of 0.02) to buy a 10.9% token reduction. Even a passing one-shot confirmation would have licensed only a narrow claim -- 'roughly 10% token savings while just inside a 2-point quality margin on this distribution' -- with essentially no generalization headroom, so a modest distribution shift would erase the operating point. The GPU cost of a qualification-style campaign was not justified by that claim.

answer_probe_cost_gate_v1.diagnosis_bottleneck_has_moved: Across EOB-v2 (action opportunity is real) -> ANSWER_PROBE_GATE_V1 (confidence has signal; learned controller fails) -> V2 (class-design/instrument defect found and fixed) -> cost-aware development (objective made well-posed; frontier measured), the binding constraint has moved from training-data quantity to OBSERVABILITY. Confidence alone cannot observe whether relevant external evidence exists, which is precisely the quantity the escalation decision depends on. The ~38.6pp of unreached, quality-free cost savings is the quantitative justification for adding one cheap sensing stage rather than more data or a larger model.

answer_probe_cost_gate_v1.recommended_resolution_pending_research_: Operationalize the SAME frozen preference ordering ('maximize quality; among quality-tied policies prefer cheaper') as a two-part NON-INFERIORITY test rather than one compressed scalar: (1) quality non-inferior to the best fixed policy within a prospectively frozen margin, AND (2) strictly lower mean compute with a positive grouped-bootstrap LCB on the compute saving. This requires no exchange rate between quality and compute -- the thing lexicographic was chosen to avoid -- while producing an effect size a bootstrap can actually resolve (the oracle's 40% token reduction). It is a faithful restatement of the already-frozen preference ordering, not a new one, but it IS a protocol revision made after seeing PHASE_3 and must therefore be frozen and then tested once on a fresh split.

attainability_frontier_dev_holdout.reading: The quality/compute frontier is STEEP and the gate captures only a small share of the oracle's headroom. At zero quality loss the gate saves just 1.4% of tokens (tau<=0.40); reaching 10% costs ~1.5 quality points; 32% costs ~8.9. The ORACLE by contrast reaches 40% at ZERO quality loss. So the probe has real signal (PHASE_2, |d| up to 0.56) but not enough precision to identify the memory-won't-help tasks cleanly -- that gap between 1.4% and 40% at zero loss is the honest measure of how far confidence-only gating falls short of the information an oracle has.

v1_1_revision.change: Replaced the compressed lexicographic scalar with a two-part non-inferiority test operationalizing the SAME preference ordering: ESCALATE iff P_hat(memory improves quality) >= TAU, promotion requiring quality non-inferiority within 0.02 AND >=10% relative token reduction AND positive grouped-bootstrap LCB on the saving AND the carried-over safety bound AND the carried-over class floors.

SEPARATION_STOPGATE_RESULT.reading: The cheap ANSWER_NOW probe's own confidence DOES carry real action-value information -- MEMORY-needed tasks are answered with measurably lower confidence than ANSWER-sufficient tasks. Per protocol, training proceeded (was not skipped).

TRAINED_GATE_RESULT.reading: E3 (the trained logistic gate) underperforms BOTH E1 (always escalate) and E2 (a single fixed confidence threshold) on held-out eval, and its LCB is deeply negative. The dangerous asymmetric error is severe: P(ACCEPT | MEMORY would improve)=0.7778 -- the trained gate confidently withholds escalation on 7/9 held-out cases where memory was actually needed, worse than the trivial always-escalate policy would have done on those same cases by construction.

evidence.contrast_with_the_real_regime: MEMORY_required (where memory genuinely executes): 744/750 non-empty packets and a 262-to-0 strict-win split -- completely one-directional. That is what a real action-value effect looks like in this instrument.

evidence.split_is_indistinguishable_from_a_coin_f: V2: 13 ANSWER_strict_win vs 6 MEMORY_strict_win over 19 discordant pairs, exact two-sided binomial p=0.167. Inspecting the outputs confirms it: A1's losses are hallucinated near-miss variants ('Nigerian franc', 'Kuwaiti riyal', 'Moroccan franc') and A1's wins are the mirror image ('Estonian krona' -> 'Estonia euro'), i.e. resampling, not evidence use.

POST_HOC_DIAGNOSTIC_answer_strict_win_is.therefore_the_actual_blocker: Not hand-verified-GK-fact supply, and not GPU compute. It is the absence of any task family that BOTH (a) makes CERTIFIED_MEMORY_V1 genuinely execute against real evidence and (b) has memory genuinely degrade a correct direct answer, using phrasing the REAL extract_subject/extract_target_relation and grammar_v4 entity extractor accept with zero bypass. Constructing that is a real open problem: GK questions parse natively, but grammar_v4's entity regex (Capitalized head + 1-3 lowercase words) cannot bind a single-token real-world subject like 'France' in evidence prose without capturing trailing junk ('France is'), which then fails exact-entity matching against the question's canonical subject. Resolving it requires either extending the certified parser (which would change CERTIFIED_MEMORY_V1 and force re-qualification + re-confirmation) or an explicitly certified pre-parsed interface for that regime -- a decision for the research lead, not an implementation detail.
POST_HOC_DIAGNOSTIC_answer_strict_win_is.where_the_real_answer_strict_win_signal_: EOB-v1/v2's D2 (both-sufficient) and D3 (memory-distractor) regimes, already measured and replicated: Q fell from 0.75 to 0.37 (D2) and 0.75 to 0.13 (D3), with D3 showing a 64% strict-ANSWER-win rate in BOTH independent runs. That is a large, one-directional, replicated 'memory actively hurts' effect -- the genuine article. It was excluded from executive TRAINING data because D2/D3 required the privileged-parsing bypass (see PRIVILEGED_PARSING_SCOPE_CAVEAT on eob_v2_opportunity_study), which the research lead ruled out for training data.

b3_retrieval_calibration.CAVEAT_not_comparable_to_confirmation_1: cal_2200 shows CES@50 = 0.633 whereas confirmation #1 at a nearly identical N=2224 showed 0.412. The gap is a design consequence, not a contradiction: calibration grows the corpus with FILLER drawn from unrelated tasks, so the number of same-task near-duplicates and dead-ends per task stays fixed, whereas a natively-generated corpus of that size carries proportionally more confusable distractors. The suite therefore isolates raw search-space size with confusability density held roughly constant -- the cleaner isolation for measuring k(N) -- but absolute CES values must NOT be read across to confirmation #1, and any coverage target set on calibration will be optimistic relative to a natively-scaled corpus.
b3_retrieval_calibration.FINDING_1_k_star_is_sub_linear: N grew 4.29x (700 -> 3000) while MEDIAN k* grew only 1.25x (28 -> 35). k* is strongly SUB-LINEAR in N, far closer to constant than proportional. This directly challenges the linear k = ceil(rho*N) form the protocol permits: a fixed fraction would over-provision badly at large N.
b3_retrieval_calibration.FINDING_2_fraction_does_not_stabilise_co: median k*/N FALLS monotonically with N (0.0400, 0.0305, 0.0227, 0.0146, 0.0117) rather than holding constant, and p90 k*/N is unstable across scales (0.267, 0.598, 0.283, 0.311, 0.372). b4_candidate_compression.P3_RESULT_compression_is_viable: The oracle compressor recovers strongly: end-to-end selected CES 0.620/0.540/0.507/0.513/0.473 at M=25, versus P1's 0.353/0.287/0.153/0.160/0.120 and P0's 0.493/0.393/0.387/0.320/0.340. So a perfect compressor lets UNCHANGED S2 both keep the availability B3 bought AND select from it -- roughly 1.4x the k=50 baseline at every scale, and 3-4x P1 at the large scales. Compression is the right shape of intervention, and S2 is not irreparably broken.
b4_candidate_compression.diagnosis: The two-opposing-quantities scoring did its job: it separated 'reduced pressure' from 'kept the evidence' and showed my compressor achieves the first by sacrificing the second. Structure-as-admissibility was too coarse a filter -- 'mentions the subject OR the relation OR a one-hop entity OR looks like an identity record' admits far more than M records at these pool sizes, so the retrieval-score ranking inside the admitted set decides what survives, and retrieval score is precisely the signal that already failed to rank the bridge highly. The compressor inherits the retriever's blind spot rather than correcting it.
b4_candidate_compression.next: Either a better runtime-safe discriminator (relation-typed matching, subject-anchored path scoring, role-aware reservation) or the runtime graph. P3 gives the ceiling to beat and P2 gives the floor a new mechanism must clear.
b4_candidate_compression.per_frozen_decision_rule: 'P3 succeeds but P2 fails -> compression is viable; the runtime-safe compressor needs better discrimination.' Recorded as exactly that. Not a licence to widen M, weaken the bound, or raise the packet.
b4_candidate_compression.status: P3 SUCCEEDS, P2 FAILS. Per the frozen decision rule: compression is VIABLE, but the runtime-safe compressor needs better discrimination. No arm promoted, no HRM run.
b4_candidate_compression.what_this_says_about_the_graph: P3 proves a compressor that KNOWS which records matter unlocks S2. The runtime cannot know that from retrieval score plus coarse structural admissibility. A runtime graph is precisely a mechanism for identifying which records matter STRUCTURALLY rather than by score -- reaching the bridge by relation-aware traversal instead of hoping it ranks well. The P3-minus-P2 gap (0.473 vs 0.340 at cal_3000) is now a measured budget for what better discrimination is worth.

root_cause_diagnosed.mechanism: RECORD_EXPRESSES_RELATION is a substring match of the question's parsed relation phrase against record text -- the same weak completeness signal G1_TYPED_PATH and B4's coarse prefilter also use. Those two mechanisms survive its weakness because both degrade to filling remaining M capacity with retrieval-rank filler, which passively recovers many true terminal records that the relation-text match misses. G2 deliberately removes that filler (M is a ceiling, not a target -- the correction the user specified), which removes the safety net along with the padding: real working-set sizes collapsed to 7-25 records against a 25/50/75 ceiling, and paths_complete averaged only 1.6-3.1 per task against 9-39 enumerated, so most of what G2 found was structurally plausible but relation-incomplete, and got ranked below the tiny complete set without ever reaching the working set.
root_cause_diagnosed.not_a_ranking_problem: paths_enumerated and unique_bridge_entities both climb with scale (9.5->38.6 and 3.7->17.9), so the graph IS finding bridges. headline_finding.claim: K3 (the oracle ceiling, restricted to records the SAME topology walk K0/K1 already reach) barely beats K0 at all.
headline_finding.meaning: Even a PERFECT completion recognizer -- one that never mislabels a single record -- could not have closed more than 0.7-1.3 percentage points of working-set CES, because the records it would need to label correctly are usually not reachable by the graph's 1-2 hop co-mention walk in the first place. R_endpoint for K3 is 1.000 at every scale by construction (it always recognizes what it can reach); R_endpoint for K0/K1 is only 0.06-0.10. That gap looks large in isolation, but the DENOMINATOR it operates on (topology-reachable required records) is small and mostly overlaps with what K0's loose substring match already recovers through partial-tier admission -- G2 does not pad the working set, so partial (non-complete) records still enter it whenever total candidates are below M, which they almost always are here (working sets averaged 6-25 records against ceilings of 25-75).

g2_v2_path_completion.next_diagnostic_question: Why is the 1-2 hop co-mention topology so sparse relative to required evidence? Candidates: (a) the corpus's multi-hop chains route through bridges that are NOT co-mentioned with the subject in any single record (i.e. the true link is a chain of separate facts, not a shared record), (b) entity extraction (extract_v4_entities) fails to recognize the SAME entity across records due to surface-form variance, fragmenting what should be one node into several, or (c) the candidate pool depth (C2 expanded k) doesn't retrieve the specific bridge/endpoint records at all, independent of graph construction. g2_v2_path_completion.why_this_overturns_the_g2_v1_diagnosis: G2-v1 attributed the failure to completion RECOGNITION (a record wasn't being labeled complete even though it should have been). This sprint's K3 arm falsifies that: recognition was never the binding constraint. The actual constraint is REACHABILITY -- required records frequently sit outside the 1-2 hop subject/bridge co-mention neighborhood the runtime graph walks at all, so no completion rule, however accurate, can recover them. K1's entity-bound recognizer IS more correct than K0 in isolation (see tests/unit/test_g2_endpoint_recognition.py -- it correctly rejects wrong-entity bindings K0 falsely accepts, and correctly recognizes value-shaped records the older relational_state.py parser missed entirely). This is cosmetic, NOT a connectivity defect: alias_links is keyed independently of records_by_entity, so connectivity is unaffected (R_connectivity=1.0).
FINDING_1_IDENTITY_HYPOTHESIS_FALSIFIED.conclusion: The existing extract_identity_links/alias_links machinery works PERFECTLY on this corpus: every identity record is in the pool, parsed correctly, emits a bidirectional alias edge, and successfully connects the canonical entity to the question anchor. A PERFECT ORACLE canonical merge (the I1 arm here is an oracle ceiling, not a runtime repair) produces EXACTLY ZERO improvement in per-task reachability. G2-v4I is not merely deprioritized -- it is falsified. Do not build the CanonicalEntityNode architecture.

FINDING_2_BRIDGE_ACQUISITION_REAL_BUT_MO.conclusion: 68.1% of missing bridge records are merely just past the pool cutoff -- a budget/acquisition-policy problem, the cheap end of the spectrum. Only 29.7% are genuinely unranked (the architectural, graph-guided-retrieval case). Fusion displacement is negligible (2.2%), so bridge-preserving fusion is NOT warranted.

FINDING_3_NEW_DOMINANT_CAUSE_DISCONNECTE.conclusion: 40% of terminal records are in the pool, extract entities fine, but sit in a DIFFERENT connected component from the anchor. Deeper traversal does not fix this (beyond-hop-bound is only 6.5%, and the verified hop curve gains just +2.4pp/+7.5pp past h=2). This is now the largest single defect.

FINDING_4_THE_DISCONNECTION_DECOMPOSES_F.probe: For every disconnected in-pool terminal record, asked whether any of its extracted entities is a NEAR-MISS (substring either direction) of an entity the BFS actually reached.
FINDING_4_THE_DISCONNECTION_DECOMPOSES_F.root_cause_of_the_near_misses: extract_v4_entities' _STOP_LAST trailing-token list is incomplete. It strips 'is/was/has/registered/assigned/paired/applies/...' but NOT 'resolves', 'uses', 'set', 'value', 'maps', 'requires'. The extractor therefore emits 'jacana control module resolves' as a DISTINCT entity node from 'jacana control module', fragmenting the graph -- not because of any alias/abbreviation problem, but because of a stop-word gap.
FINDING_4_THE_DISCONNECTION_DECOMPOSES_F.significance: ~19.4% of ALL terminal records (40% disconnected x 48.6% near-miss) are disconnected purely because of an incomplete stop-word list. That is a one-line-scale fix with a large expected effect, and it is entity-boundary normalisation, NOT the typed-relation-edge work that the prior (buggy) topology reading would have motivated.

bug_found.description: oracle_targets in scripts/diagnose_g2_v3_reachability.py was built from task._oracle_metadata.surfaces['subject'] and ['bridge'] only, omitting ['canonical']. For abbreviation-regime tasks (entity_regime='abbreviation'), surfaces['subject'] is the QUESTION's own surface form (e.g. 'BCM-3'), not the canonical form most evidence records actually use ('Bittern control module', in surfaces['canonical']). headline_finding.meaning: Required evidence overwhelmingly fails to reach S2 not because it's unretrieved (R0=7.3%), not because it's structurally distant (R4 >2-hop=4.2%), not because ranking/completion mis-scores it once found (R6+R7=6.8%), but because the SAME real-world entity is represented as different, unmerged graph nodes depending on which surface form (canonical, abbreviation, alias) a given record happens to use.

r2_subclassification.conclusion: The dominant failure is real, not a diagnostic or extraction artifact. Identity-role records (surface->canonical mapping records, e.g. 'JPA-5 is the short code for X') are 100% genuine fragmentation by construction -- their entire purpose is to state a DIFFERENT surface form, and the runtime's own alias-resolution mechanism (extract_identity_links -> graph.alias_links) is failing to connect most of them into the subject's component despite existing for exactly this purpose.
r2_subclassification.purpose: Distinguish extraction-boundary noise (cheap fix: extract_v4_entities' greedy regex over/under-captures the SAME mention) from genuine cross-surface fragmentation (structural: alias/abbreviation with zero textual overlap, requires real canonicalization/node-merging work) -- added mid-sprint before freezing the conclusion, since a 60%+ R2 rate on terminal records could plausibly have been mostly the former.

E1_EXCEEDS_E2_AND_WHY_THAT_IS_NOT_A_CONT.explanation: The E2 oracle arm was scoped to truncate ONLY extractions that begin with an oracle-known surface (subject/canonical/bridge). It therefore does not repair boundary errors on other entities -- distractors, decoys, unrelated records -- which nonetheless participate in graph connectivity as intermediate nodes. E1's grammar rule repairs every entity uniformly. So E2 is a NARROWER intervention than E1, not a true upper bound on boundary repair.
E1_EXCEEDS_E2_AND_WHY_THAT_IS_NOT_A_CONT.honest_reading: Do not report this as 'beating the oracle'. It means the E2 ceiling was mis-scoped as an upper bound: a correctly-scoped boundary oracle would have to fix all entities, at which point it would equal or exceed E1. The comparison still validates E1 (closure >= 1.0 against the best available boundary reference), but the ceiling itself should be re-derived if it is ever needed as a hard bound.

RESULTS.headline: A single grammar-aware boundary rule lifts per-task reachability from 51.1% to 84.4% (+33.3pp), with bridge-record connectivity going to 100% and terminal to 86.7%. This is far larger than the ~19pp estimated from the near-miss share alone, because boundary fragmentation was also silently breaking connectivity through non-required intermediate entities.

FINDING_5_FOUR_STAGE_DECOMPOSITION_the_s.reading: Availability rose enormously at every upstream stage -- bridge working-set survival 55.4% -> 100%, terminal 36.7% -> 74.7%, graph reachability 75.4% -> 100% and 44.7% -> 79.3%. This is precisely the B3/B4 pressure-reintroduction pattern: more records survive to the working set, so S2 faces more competition and keeps a smaller FRACTION of them. End-to-end still improved because the availability gain outweighed the retention loss, but the binding constraint has now moved decisively into S2 selection.

FROZEN_CONCLUSION.gpu_spent: NONE on this branch. The probe requires no model generation, so PHASE_1 and PHASE_2/3A ran entirely on CPU, and the frozen stop condition fired before any evaluation split was built or any credit was spent.
FROZEN_CONCLUSION.statement: A cheap retrieval probe -- C2 retrieval plus identity binding, run before the escalation decision and reusing its result on escalation -- does not add deployment-transferable information about whether full memory is worth invoking, on this instrument. Its apparent incremental discrimination over direct-answer confidence within MEMORY_required (Delta_AUC +0.0566) is 86% attributable to a corpus-size indicator that is constant in any single-corpus deployment. Controlling for it, the gain is +0.0229 with a negative lower confidence bound, and the within-scale control gives +0.0034. The retrieval features that would genuinely transfer -- top-1 score, top-k mean, score margin -- contribute -0.0006.
FROZEN_CONCLUSION.what_this_does_and_does_not_close: It closes THIS probe's feature set on THIS instrument. It does not establish that no cheap observation could work -- but it does rule out the specific, natural candidate (retrieval strength/margin/binding), and it shows the fused RRF scores do not distinguish 'the answer is present' from 'nothing relevant is present' within a b3 corpus. Any richer probe would need to inspect whether retrieved records actually carry the target relation for the bound subject, which begins to approach doing the memory work itself -- the circularity the availability taxonomy exists to prevent.

VERDICT_SUPERSEDED.what_was_wrong: Restricting to MEMORY_required removed the EMPTY-POOL shortcut but left a second, subtler one. probe_candidate_count = c2(corpus_size) = min(300, ceil(0.15*n)) is a DETERMINISTIC function of which of the five exec_training_v2 scales a task came from -- exactly one distinct value per scale (105/150/225/300/300) -- and those scales differ sharply in how often memory helps (0.453 at exec2_700 down to 0.233 at exec2_2200). VERDICT_SUPERSEDED.why_it_cannot_transfer: Against ONE fixed corpus -- the deployment condition -- retrieval depth is a constant, so probe_candidate_count is a constant and can predict nothing. Its apparent power here is an artifact of this benchmark spanning five corpus sizes of differing difficulty.

FINDING_1_dominant_failure_is_WRONG_PATH.reading: Of required records that ARE present in the working set but do not reach the packet, ~64% are lost because S2 prefers a COMPETING complete path. FINDING_2_path_coherent_composition_clos.reading: Admitting the highest-ranked COMPLETE path's records first -- changing nothing about ranking, retrieval, graph, or working set -- raises selected CES 0.323 -> 0.528, more than doubles bridge retention (0.183 -> 0.423) and more than doubles complete-path retention (0.217 -> 0.503). This is the single largest selection-side lever found.

FINDING_3_redundancy_is_NOT_the_problem.reading: Suppressing duplicate structural signatures eliminates redundancy entirely (0.57 -> 0.00) and makes selected CES slightly WORSE. Redundancy collision accounts for only 3.1% of failures. A diversity/dedup fix is ruled out.

FINDING_4_role_reservation_helps_but_onl.reading: Reserving one slot per runtime-inferred role recovers 19.3% of the gap, almost entirely through TERMINAL retention (0.497 -> 0.614). Bridge retention slightly DROPS (0.183 -> 0.168), because a reserved terminal slot can displace the bridge. Role balance is a real but secondary factor, and less than half as valuable as path coherence.

FINDING_5_large_selection_side_headroom_.reading: Perfect selection on the SAME G2/E1 working sets reaches 0.793 vs the current 0.323. The working sets already contain far more usable evidence than S2 extracts. Selection, not availability, is where the remaining value is.

sprint_a_retrieval_diagnosis.method: Frozen receipts truncate bm25_ranked/bge_ranked/fusion_ranked at the candidate budget (50), so a required record at true rank 73 is indistinguishable from one at rank 2000 -- both merely absent. sprint_a_retrieval_diagnosis.plan_phases_this_affects: Phases 4-7 of the repair plan (structured query builder, role-aware retrieval passes, terminal-answer retrieval optimization, temporal query handling) were premised on required evidence being absent from retrieval. It is not absent -- it is ranked and truncated. Those phases may still be worth doing to raise evidence RANK (so it survives a tight budget), which is a different and more precisely stated objective than raising recall. Recommend re-scoping them around rank improvement plus the two separable repairs above, before building new retrieval mechanisms.

Phase 7's temporal sub-experiment should therefore start by asking why temporal records rank low under a tight budget, not by adding temporal representation machinery.
temporal_chain_reframed.previous_reading: temporal_chain candidate CES 0.060 looked like a representation failure needing temporal embeddings / graph machinery.

the_generalization_artifact.interpretation: At equal ABSOLUTE budget the dev->qual gap is -13% to -32%. At equal corpus FRACTION the gap is +3.3% to -1.8%, i.e. indistinguishable. Retrieval's ranking quality generalizes essentially perfectly; the measured collapse is an artifact of holding a fixed absolute candidate budget (50) while the corpus grew 4.15x. This substantially revises the assumed repair: the retrieval lane is primarily a budget/pool-sizing question, not a query-reformulation or representation-learning question.

1_fusion_displacement_budget_neutral.finding: RRF discards required evidence that a single retriever already had INSIDE the budget: 88/370 qualification misses (23.8%), 7/29 development misses (24.1%). Of the qualification cases BM25 had 61 inside budget (median rank 37) and BGE had 27 (median rank 42).
1_fusion_displacement_budget_neutral.why_it_matters: This is recoverable WITHOUT enlarging the candidate pool, so it does not change what the selector must cope with. Cheapest available retrieval win and the one to test first.

2_budget_scaling_needs_a_protocol_versio.critical_unmeasured_interaction: Raising k is NOT established as a net win. A larger pool means more distractors for a selector already shown to drop 48% of AVAILABLE evidence (and to over-expand specifically on EXACT-identity tasks). Availability and final quality can move in opposite directions here. This interaction must be MEASURED on development before any budget change is frozen -- do not assume bigger k improves Q.
2_budget_scaling_needs_a_protocol_versio.finding: The remaining 76% of misses are genuinely below the cutoff and need a larger (or corpus-relative) budget.
2_budget_scaling_needs_a_protocol_versio.open_design_question: Whether the candidate budget should be corpus-relative rather than a fixed absolute constant. A fraction generalizes across these two corpora but will not scale to natural corpora where a fixed fraction of millions of documents is meaningless. Needs an explicit design decision, frozen in the new protocol, not a tuned constant.

RESOLVED is left untouched. Protection consumes one slot of the SAME packet budget.
sprint_b2_selector_repair.leakage_discipline: Eligibility reads only record content, the relation parsed from the question, identity.canonical, and frozen fusion score/rank. record_kind is forbidden -- its values are generator answer-key labels. Enforced by a test that strips docstrings and asserts no executable statement touches record_kind/proof_edges/latent_bridge/answer_node/required_evidence_ids, plus a guard-the-guard test.

C11_crash_recovery.commit_sequence: append event -> fsync -> derive incrementally -> atomically publish snapshot (temp -> fsync -> os.replace)

partial snapshot temp file never published

C11_crash_recovery.recovery_rule_implemented: A snapshot is only ever an accelerator. It records the corpus_version and log sha256 it was derived from, and is DISCARDED AND REBUILT on any mismatch. A gap was found and fixed during implementation: load replayed correctly but did not republish a missing/invalid snapshot, so 'discarded then rebuilt' was only half-implemented.

verified_memory_consolidation_v1.alias_handling: Clusters from EXPLICIT alias_of claims only -- never string similarity, co-occurrence or embeddings, since inferring identity is a truth decision. Ingest-time conflict detection stays local (raw key); alias-aware grouping is global and consolidation-only. They may disagree by design: a later alias claim can reveal a contradiction invisible at ingest.

headline_invariant_C9.checked_at_every_step: Asserted after EVERY event, not only at the end, so a divergence cannot be masked by a later compensating change.
headline_invariant_C9.specific_bug_class_covered: test_retraction_dissolves_groups_identically_in_both_paths -- a retracted record left behind in a support/contradiction/duplicate group is the most likely consolidation bug, and the contradiction group is asserted to dissolve entirely.

verified_memory_consolidation_v1.next: Pressure test at 100k-1M synthetic events (new claims, duplicates, aliases, conflicts, supersessions, retractions), measuring replay time, incremental latency, active count, index size, memory, retrieval correctness, drift at checkpoints, and cache invalidation. Reported as measurements with NO frozen performance threshold -- inventing one after seeing the numbers would be post-hoc. O(n) full replay is expected to dominate as the log grows; if it does, that is the finding motivating a later checkpoint/compaction design.
verified_memory_consolidation_v1.not_a_quality_claim: CAPABILITY and CORRECTNESS milestone. No quality gate was run and none is implied.

pre_pressure_test_fix.finding: A scaling probe run BEFORE the ladder found the write path was O(n^2): per-event cost doubled with every doubling of n (1.03ms at 500 events -> 5.79ms at 4k), extrapolating to roughly 16 DAYS for 1M events.
pre_pressure_test_fix.fixes: raw-claim-key index of active records; running log hash updated per appended line; manifest writing moved to travel with snapshot publication rather than firing per event.
pre_pressure_test_fix.result: flat ~74us/event, ratio ~1.00x across 500..8000 -- genuinely O(n). 77x faster at 4k, widening with scale.
three_separate_causes: ingest scanned retrievable() to find conflicting claims -- O(n) per event
log_sha256() re-read and re-hashed the ENTIRE log on every append -- O(n) bytes per event
_write_manifest() recomputed state_counts and a full consolidated snapshot on every append
pre_pressure_test_fix.why_this_was_safe: All 43 write+consolidation tests still pass, and C9 (incremental == full replay) is what makes 'semantics unchanged' a checkable claim rather than an assertion. Correctness before performance is what allowed the optimization at all.

pressure_test_result.against_the_frozen_criterion: 1M events rebuild in ~19s -- 'tens of seconds' -- so checkpoint compaction is NOT yet required for replay TIME. Memory footprint and the absence of any fast-start path are the real constraints.
pressure_test_result.fsync_caveat: os.fsync on darwin does not force a physical device flush (F_FULLFSYNC would), so durability numbers are optimistic relative to Linux.

harness_defect_found_and_corrected.consequence: Those three rows are ONE measurement repeated, not a scale sweep, and must not be read as evidence that restart cost is scale-independent.
harness_defect_found_and_corrected.correction: scripts/measure_restart_recovery.py measures it properly by truncating a copy of the canonical log to each scale, which is valid precisely because C12 established the log is append-only and prefix-stable.
harness_defect_found_and_corrected.defect: The recovery sweep inside pressure_test_verified_memory.py reopened the SAME store after the ladder had already grown to 1M, so all three rows measured a 1M cold replay while being labelled 100k/500k/1M (22.87s / 22.99s / 21.29s -- near-identical, which is the tell).

pressure_test_result.headline: INTEGRITY (incremental == full replay) held TRUE at EVERY rung including 1M. Ingestion is FLAT at 67-79 us/event across three orders of magnitude (~13,600 events/sec sustained), i.e. genuinely O(n) overall.
pressure_test_result.memory_is_the_binding_constraint: RSS grows linearly at ~5.1 MB per 1k events, reaching 5.14 GB at 1M. This is a SEPARATE defect from the O(n^2) one fixed above: ClaimStore retains BOTH _events (every raw event dict) and _records in RAM, roughly doubling the footprint for no benefit since the log is already on disk. Named explicitly rather than folded into a general 'memory is high'.
pressure_test_result.replay_scaling_caveat: Full replay is broadly linear but shows mild superlinearity at the top: 6.95s at 500k -> 19.03s at 1M is 2.74x for a 2x increase. Most plausibly allocation/GC pressure at ~5 GB RSS rather than an algorithmic term; not investigated further, and reported as observed rather than explained away.

restart_recovery_corrected.PRIMARY_FINDING: The snapshot does NOT accelerate startup. All three startup paths -- no snapshot, valid snapshot, invalidated snapshot -- take the same time (max relative gap 9.6%, i.e. noise), because ClaimStore.__init__ ALWAYS replays the full log and uses snapshot_is_valid() only to decide whether to republish. Restart cost is therefore unavoidably O(n), and the snapshot machinery is currently pure overhead for startup.
restart_recovery_corrected.method: truncate a copy of the canonical log to each scale and replay it -- valid precisely because C12 established the log is append-only and prefix-stable
restart_recovery_corrected.scaling: Roughly linear with the same mild superlinearity seen in the ladder (500k->1M is 2.4x time for 2x events).
restart_recovery_corrected.this_supersedes: the recovery block in pressure_test_v1.json, whose 22.87/22.99/21.29s rows were one 1M measurement repeated three times. The true sweep is linear: 1.20s -> 7.43s -> 17.78s.

what_this_answers.answer: Checkpointed replay is NOT yet required on TIME grounds -- 1M restarts in ~18s, which is operationally fine. Two other things are more pressing, and neither is background verification: (1) RSS of 5.14 GB at 1M, driven by retaining _events in RAM alongside _records when the log is already on disk -- a cheap fix that should roughly halve the footprint; (2) the snapshot currently accelerates nothing, so the fast-start path the design anticipated does not exist yet. Extrapolating, 10M events would mean ~3 minutes of replay and ~50 GB RSS, so MEMORY fails before time does.
what_this_answers.question: Is the next milestone merely background verification, or is checkpointed replay/compaction needed first?
what_this_answers.recommendation: Fix the in-memory event retention first (cheap, large win, no design change). Checkpointed replay becomes worthwhile around 10M events, or sooner if restart latency becomes user-visible. Background verification remains a separate axis and is not blocked by either.

the_false_pass_hazard_was_real_and_is_no.T6_demonstrates_it_is_real: get_cached_backend returns the IDENTICAL backend object for two record sets with the same evidence_id but DIFFERENT content. The hazard is demonstrated, not assumed.
the_false_pass_hazard_was_real_and_is_no.architectural_consequence: An 'update' is always a new record plus supersession of the old, never an in-place content edit -- which is the same thing the never-silently-delete policy requires. The two constraints agree.
the_false_pass_hazard_was_real_and_is_no.hazard: The certified reader caches retrieval backends under (mode, frozenset(evidence_id)) -- a CONTENT-BLIND key. A write could succeed, the store could be correct, and retrieval could silently answer from a stale index.
the_false_pass_hazard_was_real_and_is_no.why_it_is_unreachable_here: record_id is provenance-addressed (sha256 of content|source|observed_at), so any change to what a record says produces a different id, and the content-blind cache key necessarily changes with it. This makes content-addressing load-bearing rather than decorative -- an implementation that reused ids across a content edit would have silently failed.
